name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: Iraq's PM al-Zaidi dismissed the Maysan provincial military commander and police chief after an internal investigation confirmed the 10-11 Sep Petroline drone strikes launched from Maysan, Iraq; the Iran-backed umbrella group 'Islamic Resistance in Iraq' issued an ambiguous non-denial ('an honour we do not claim'); AP reports repair will take an estimated 3-5 weeks. The 14 Sep Salalah ministerial collapsed not merely on scheduling but because Saudi Arabia submitted amendments to the Iran-Oman shipping-lane proposal over concern its wording would lock in a new, unacceptable status quo -- Iran and Oman agreed to reschedule but no new date has been set. No further major Hormuz vessel incident this cycle.
importance: Critical — the Hormuz-bypass route and the leading multilateral diplomatic mechanism both failed within the same 72 hours, raising the sustained-risk floor for Gulf energy flows and shipping even without a single dramatic escalation.
assessment: Attribution has moved from wholly unresolved to ASSESSED Iran-aligned Iraqi-militia origin, though still formally unclaimed. The Salalah collapse is now understood as a substantive Saudi red line rather than a scheduling conflict, lowering the odds of a quick multilateral fix and elevating the relative importance of the narrower Iran-Oman bilateral track and the new Iran-UAE channel.
lastChange: 2026-09-15 -- Petroline attribution hardens (Maysan commander/police-chief dismissals, IRI non-denial); repair estimated 3-5 weeks; Salalah collapse attributed to a substantive Saudi objection, not scheduling.
orgRelevance: Treat the current disruption level as a multi-week, sustained planning assumption rather than an episodic crisis; reassess Gulf-transiting shipping, energy, and insurance exposure accordingly. Watch for Petroline repair-progress updates and any rescheduled Salalah date or Iran-Oman bilateral shipping arrangement as the nearest inflections.
nextIndicator: A formal attribution statement from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, or Iran; Petroline repair-progress reporting; a rescheduled Salalah date or an unveiled Iran-Oman bilateral shipping arrangement; further attacks during the diplomatic gap.

The 14 Sep GCC-Iran Salalah ministerial is postponed 'in the interest of consensus'; CNBC publishes satellite imagery confirming the extent of Petroline pipeline damage; a bilateral Iran-Oman shipping-lane arrangement continues to be advanced separately.

Iraq dismisses the Maysan military commander and provincial police chief after an investigation into the Petroline strikes' Iraqi origin; IRI issues a non-denial; AP reports a 3-5 week repair estimate; the Salalah ministerial collapse is confirmed to stem from a substantive Saudi objection to the Iran-Oman proposal's wording, with no reschedule date set.

DFARS 252.204-7012/7021, SPRS scores, and annual affirmations remain in force throughout.
importance: High — governs DIB compliance spend and contract-award eligibility.
assessment: Policy pause, not repeal; a reformed program and reset timeline remain the leading outcome. The public-report timeline has slipped modestly further out, extending contractors' information gap without changing the underlying obligations.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — internal determination reportedly delivered to the DoW CIO but remains non-public; realistic public-report date resets to late September/early October.
orgRelevance: Maintain 800-171 controls, SPRS currency, and C3PAO readiness through the now-slightly-extended information gap.
nextIndicator: Any Federal Register notice, solicitation-language change, or industry-day signal ahead of the public report.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's military-affiliated license-denial rule (since 1 Dec 2025) and the June 2026 entity-list targeting of MP Materials/USA Rare Earth remain the binding constraints; no new PRC action this cycle. Beijing's confirmed 23-25 Sep Xi Jinping Washington visit (24 Sep Trump meeting) is now paired with an emerging analyst consensus (CSIS, Foreign Policy, S&P Global) that the most likely deliverable is a one-year extension of the Oct 2025 Busan trade truce -- easing broader trade friction without resolving the military-affiliated rare-earth licensing denial.
importance: Critical — binding, targeted constraint on munitions/platform output and the domestic-substitution response itself, now with a confirmed summit date as the nearest potential inflection point ahead of the 10 Nov suspension-expiry decision.
assessment: Durable, weaponizable chokepoint persists unchanged through the summit's realistic 'good' outcome. A truce rollover would stabilize the broader relationship but leave defense-sector magnet exposure intact; a talks-falter scenario would harden the constraint further. Supply-chain mitigation should proceed independent of the summit outcome.
lastChange: 2026-09-15 -- no new PRC action; analyst consensus firms around a Busan-truce rollover (not rare-earth relief) as the summit's likely outcome.
orgRelevance: Continue mapping magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities and pursuing second sources without waiting on summit outcomes; treat the pre/post-summit window (through ~24-26 Sep) as a dedicated watch period for any licensing signal.
nextIndicator: Any explicit rare-earth licensing signal at or around the 24 Sep summit; the 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry decision; any further PRC entity-list action.

name: Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / AI-Infra CVEs
status: Cisco FMC exploitation attribution (Sandworm-linked and Qilin-ransomware clusters, Talos) is unchanged this cycle with ~700 instances still internet-exposed and no named DIB victim yet. The maximum-severity GitLab CE/EE path-traversal flaw (CVE-2026-85706, CVSS 10.0, added to KEV 11 Sep) has progressed from same-day proof-of-concept exploitation to confirmed exfiltration of configuration files, embedded secrets, and SSH configuration data from unpatched, internet-facing instances with at least one public project (watchTowr, Rapid7). Citrix NetScaler exploitation continues past its 12 Sep deadline without new attribution.
importance: Critical — confirmed simultaneous state-actor and top-tier-ransomware exploitation of DIB-relevant perimeter infrastructure, now joined by a maximum-severity DevOps/software-supply-chain flaw exploited within a day of disclosure.
assessment: The DevOps/software-supply-chain attack-surface trend is deepening, not plateauing: a second maximum-severity flaw in this category is now yielding directly usable credentials, distinct from and potentially more severe than a single-host compromise. DIB-relevant perimeter and DevOps infrastructure should remain presumed-targeted.
lastChange: 2026-09-15 -- GitLab CVE-2026-85706 exploitation confirmed to include secrets/SSH-configuration exfiltration, not merely file reads.
orgRelevance: Patch self-hosted GitLab CE/EE to 19.1.8/19.2.6/19.3.2+ immediately; inventory for public projects; rotate any secrets/SSH keys that could have lived in exposed config paths if unpatched since 11 Sep; continue Cisco FMC IOC hunting per Talos guidance.
nextIndicator: A confirmed DIB-sector or federal-contractor victim tied to any FMC cluster or the GitLab exploitation; further KEV adds in the DevOps/software-supply-chain category; any new Citrix NetScaler attribution.

history.note: Seven KEV additions (SonicWall, JFrog, LiteLLM, others).

name: Golden Dome Procurement
status: ~$1.75B for 36 SDA tracking satellites + up to $3.2B in space-based-interceptor awards; SHIELD IDIQ active; SDA's Tranche 1 Transport Layer A launch (21 Northrop-built satellites) remains scheduled 30 Sep from Vandenberg. The Army has moved to divest its IFPC-High Energy Laser ('Valkyrie,' ~300kW) fielding candidate, redirecting toward the Navy-led E-HEL program feeding Golden Dome's Joint Laser Warfighting System, with prototype delivery reported in the Sep-Oct 2026 timeframe.
importance: High — multi-year homeland-missile-defense demand base, now also consolidating adjacent directed-energy programs.
assessment: Transitioned from funding to procurement; incumbents on SDA/MDA vehicles advantaged. The Army-to-Navy laser-program redirection suggests DoD is converging separate service directed-energy efforts into the Golden Dome architecture rather than sustaining parallel tracks — a structural-consolidation trend worth watching for further mergers.
lastChange: 2026-09-14 — no new award this cycle; Army's Valkyrie high-energy-laser program redirected into the Navy-led E-HEL effort feeding Golden Dome's Joint Laser Warfighting System.
orgRelevance: Assess positioning on SDA/MDA vehicles; firms with legacy Army high-energy-laser involvement should assess transition risk; firms on the Navy-led E-HEL effort may see expanded scope.
nextIndicator: The 30 Sep SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A launch; Gate 2/3/4 SBI outcomes; any further program-consolidation announcements; new SHIELD task orders.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia
status: ZNPP remains on stable, restored external power. Ukrainian forces struck two major Russian oil facilities overnight 13-14 Sep, including the TANECO refinery in Tatarstan, extending the deep-strike campaign against Russian energy infrastructure further from the front; Russia launched 102 drones against Ukraine overnight 14 Sep, a lighter barrage than the 453/323-drone waves earlier in the week. Zelensky reiterated Ukraine's willingness to accept a mutual energy-strikes moratorium consistent with Trump's prior statement; the narrower 30-day energy-halt commitment remains unconfirmed as violated by a grid-specific strike.
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand; the ZNPP dimension carries independent nuclear-safety significance.
assessment: The deep-strike campaign against Russian energy infrastructure continues to expand in geographic reach (Tatarstan) even as nightly drone-barrage intensity eased somewhat versus the prior cycle's peaks. Zelensky's renewed public openness to an energy moratorium keeps that diplomatic option alive without a confirmed breakthrough.
lastChange: 2026-09-15 -- Ukrainian strikes reach the TANECO refinery in Tatarstan; lighter (102-drone) Russian overnight barrage; Zelensky reiterates energy-moratorium willingness.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; no direct organizational action. The expanding deep-strike geography and any energy-moratorium movement remain relevant to European energy-security and airspace monitoring.
nextIndicator: A confirmed strike specifically on Ukrainian power/grid infrastructure; any formal mutual energy-moratorium announcement; further deep-strike geographic expansion.

name: Identity-Verification Supply Chain Breach (IDScan.net)
status: IDScan.net's confirmed breach is now reported to have exposed identity-verification customers of Hertz, Target, FedEx, Motorola Solutions, Jack Henry, Caesars Entertainment, and over 1,000 cannabis dispensaries nationwide. Nine putative class actions were docketed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana between 2-4 Sep, growing toward the 'over a dozen' figure reported by 10 Sep; no MDL consolidation has been reported yet; the FBI investigation continues.
importance: High — resolves a prior gap (vendor unconfirmed) and confirms a systemic identity-verification supply-chain compromise with active, growing litigation and unresolved downstream-fraud exposure.
assessment: Confirms the breach's cross-sector reach extends well beyond a single industry, making document-based identity proofing a systemic fraud-enablement concern across retail, hospitality, financial services, and logistics simultaneously.
lastChange: 2026-09-15 -- named affected downstream customer categories (Hertz, Target, FedEx, Motorola Solutions, Jack Henry, Caesars, cannabis retail) confirmed; litigation count continues climbing.
orgRelevance: Directly confirm whether the organization or its KYC/onboarding vendors use IDScan.net; review contractual indemnification and breach-notification obligations.
nextIndicator: Consolidation of the class actions (e.g., an MDL); any FTC or state-AG enforcement action; confirmed downstream fraud incidents traceable to the exposed data.

name: Pentagon AI-Assisted Software Acquisition (Accelerated Mission Software / Project Gatekeeper)
status: DoD CIO Kirsten Davies signed the 'Accelerated Mission Software' instruction on 31 Aug 2026, effective 8 Sep, mandating agile DevSecOps acquisition models and directing DoD components to use AI to modernize software systems and accelerate capability delivery. A companion effort, 'Project Gatekeeper,' uses AI-assisted code evaluation to speed authorizations to operate. This lands in the same CIO organization currently synthesizing the non-public CMMC Reform Task Force determination.
importance: High -- converts AI-assisted software development from a voluntary adoption trend into formal Pentagon acquisition policy, with direct implications for contractor DevSecOps maturity and competitive positioning.
assessment: A newly formalized institutional requirement rather than an incremental adoption story. Because the same DoD CIO office is simultaneously handling CMMC reform, watch for the two acquisition-modernization tracks (software velocity and cyber-assessment scaling) to begin cross-referencing each other in future guidance.
lastChange: 2026-09-15 -- thread opened on confirmation that the Accelerated Mission Software instruction is signed and in effect, paired with the DIU's 24 Sep AI-fusion-tool solicitation deadline for space/missile threat detection.
orgRelevance: Review DevSecOps and AI-assisted code-review maturity against the new baseline for any Pentagon software-delivery capture strategy; expect solicitation language to begin referencing Project Gatekeeper-style criteria.
nextIndicator: Solicitation language referencing Project Gatekeeper or Accelerated Mission Software; follow-on CIO guidance or ATO-cycle-time metrics; outcome of DIU's 24 Sep AI-fusion-tool solicitation.
